subject: Request: resource pledge for late-stage Apexity deployment
messages:
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@apexity.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@apexity.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: resource pledge for late-stage Apexity deployment

Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re very close to final internal approvals and expect to sign a 12‑month contract by mid‑December subject to two operational asks: 1) a short-term dedicated capacity pledge at contract signature to guarantee latency for our Q1 launch, and 2) a mapping plan for sustained Dedicated capacity (throughput + regional placement).

We put together a rough estimate (attached) of requested capacity for the first 90 days. High-level ask:
- 16 GPUs (preferably H100-class) reserved as a soft pledge for 90 days beginning at signature
- Allow burst to hosted pool for peak inference windows (we expect a 2–3x traffic spike for first 2 weeks)
- Dedicated pool in us-west with fallback to us-east if needed

Can Redwood confirm provisional availability and any gating items on your side? We’re okay with a provisional commitment subject to final MSA language.

Attachments: Apexity_capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx, high-level MLP sizing notes.

Best,
Alex Wu
CTO, Apexity
alex.wu@apexity.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

Alex —

Appreciate the summary and the attachment. Congrats on getting this far. We can absolutely support a provisional pledge; to give you a firm answer we need a few quick clarifications from your side:
- Peak sequence length and typical response size (tokens)
- Expected concurrent requests at 95th pct during launch day and steady state
- Whether you need preemptible vs pinned instances (impacting our ability to reuse capacity)

Tentative internal note: based on the spreadsheet, we can provision a soft pledge of 16 GPUs for a 90‑day runway (mix to be confirmed after infra check). We’ll route a capacity availability check and propose a standby allocation policy (soft-hold -> committed on signature).

Can we schedule a 30 min call Monday to lock the mutual action plan and MSA timeline? If you can share the final model artifact size (or a rough TF32/FP16 memory footprint) that will speed our sizing.

Thanks,

Team — forwarding request from Apexity (DL-4729). They want a provisional pledge: 16 GPUs for 90 days, us-west preference, burst to hosted pool for spikes. They’re willing to accept a soft-hold until MSA executes.

Ask: can someone run an availability snapshot across dedicated pools and recommend a minimal config we can pledge today? Priorities:
- Confirm 90d soft-hold feasibility in us-west (no SLA yet)
- Propose a fallback region and model of burst-to-hosted with expected cost multiplier
- Flag any impact to existing planned commitments through Jan/Feb (we’re tight on H100s)

Aditya — would you take lead on fleet snapshot + recommended standby allocation? Marcus — if we need to re-fingerprint any planned commits, flag me. Monica — please prep a short note on contractual gating (MSA timing, credit terms + any billing comfort language).

Forwarded message attached and attachments from Apexity.

— Marissa
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 13:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: resource pledge for late-stage Apexity deployment

Marissa / team — I pulled a rapid fleet snapshot and options. See attached CSV (fleet_snapshot_nov21.csv) for counts by pool/region. TL;DR:

Current availability (as of 2026-11-21 13:30 PST):
- us-west dedicated pools: 10 H100-equivalent nodes free; 6 A100-equivalent nodes free
- us-east dedicated pools: 8 A100-equivalent nodes free
- Hosted spare capacity (best-effort burst): sufficient, but cold-start latency and token-costs increase during heavy burst

Recommendation for pledge mechanics:
1) Soft-pledge: reserve 12 GPUs in us-west (mix: 8 H100 + 4 A100) for 90 days as a soft-hold. This protects launch runway while leaving minimal headroom for other late-stage deals.
2) Burst plan: configure automatic routing to hosted pool for +2x traffic, with a pre-agreed cost uplift (roughly +20% unit cost during burst windows) and a throttle policy to protect core latency SLOs.
3) Fallback: failover to us-east (up to 8 A100) if us-west degrades — note cross-region data egress and added latency (~30–50ms).
4) Escrow / commit trigger: convert soft-pledge to committed capacity on DocuSign MSA execution or on a confirmed purchase order.

Operational caveats:
- If Apexity requires pinned, non-preemptible H100 reservation, we can do it but it will reduce our pool flexibility and increase cost; recommend soft-hold + committed upgrade at MSA.
- If we push more than 16 GPUs into standby we risk impacting an upcoming Q1 renewal for another customer (I flagged the overlap with scheduled provisioning).

Next steps: I’ll open a short capacity hold ticket in the ops tracker and schedule a 1‑hour runbook review with infra to lock routing rules.

Attachments: fleet_snapshot_nov21.csv, quick_cost_estimate.txt

— Aditya
Senior Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

Alex —

Following internal checks, we can offer a provisional soft-pledge: 12 GPUs in us-west (8 H100 + 4 A100) for 90 days, with burst-to-hosted for spikes and failover to us-east if required. Aditya noted the tradeoffs for pinned vs soft-hold — our recommendation is soft-hold until MSA executes, at which point we’ll convert to a committed allocation per the DocuSign.

If that aligns with your expectations I’ll ask legal to route the revised MSA (we’ll add the standby pledge language and the burst cost uplift clause). Can we lock a call Monday 11/23 10:00am PT to finalize the mutual action plan and sign timeline?

Thanks, and congrats again on the close.

Best,
Marissa Cole
